column1: # The draws of prompt-hook.scale-* and prompt-hook.rows-* in hook-latency.txt, one row per timed call.
# Machine: Intel Xeon Processor, CPU family 6 model 207, 8 CPUs, 1 socket of 8 cores, 1 thread per core.
# The machine has an L3 of 320 MiB and 47 GiB of memory, under Kernel-based Virtual Machine (KVM) full virtualization, on Linux 6.12.94+.
# Pinning: none; no CPU affinity was set, the guest exposes no frequency governor, and nothing else ran during the draws.
# ljos: 0.37.0 on rustc 1.89.0 (29483883e 2025-08-04), built by `cargo build --release -p ljos --bin ljos`.
# The workspace sets no [profile.release], so cargo's release defaults hold: opt-level 3, no debug info, no link-time optimization, 16 codegen units.
# Builds: c5aba8c is develop before ljos-m6b6, 4cdaab0 is ljos-m6b6, and 81f545d is lane-ljos-7sdc.
# The lane's commits are named by the shas they had before the lane was rebased onto develop 97d3ae6.
# packsetd: 0.17.3 (947c4985), packset's default release build, without packset-embed, so the writer ranks by words alone.
# Packs: scripts/terra/hook_scale.py filled the workspace seat to 1000 and to 10000 live lessons.
# Each pack was snapshotted once and copied for each draw.
# A draw copies the snapshot, starts a writer on its own port, and warms it with one /v1/search.
# It then times 3 cold prompts, each in a fresh home.
# One untimed prompt then primes the warm home.
# It then times 7 warm prompts in that home, each in a fresh session, and 8 prompts at once there.
# It then times 3 `ljos search` and stops the writer.
# Prompts: prompt k is the lesson of case random.Random(1000 + k).randrange(live), as hook_scale.py writes it.
# Cold prompts and `ljos search` use prompt 0; warm prompt i and burst call i use prompt i.
# Order: 8 blocks, so each build keeps at least 6 draws a size if two fail.
# Each block draws every (size, build) once, in an order shuffled by Python's random.SystemRandom.
# wall_ms: wall time of the call in the parent, by time.perf_counter.
# A burst row's wall_ms runs from the start of the first of its 8 calls to the end of the last.
# Stage columns: the ms of LJOS_HOOK_TIMING's hook-timing lines, summed over a stage's lines, or - where the call printed none.
# rerank_walked: the claims the rerank stage printed it walked, or - where a build prints no count.
# out: the first 12 hex digits of the sha256 of stdout; a burst row's covers its 8 outputs in prompt order.
# `ljos search` prints a score that decays with a claim's age, so its out moves between draws.
# Run back to back on one writer at each size on prompt 0, the three builds printed the same lines past that score.
# That score moved in its fourth decimal.
# hook-latency.txt takes each draw's median of its calls of a kind, then the median and quartiles of the 8 draws.
# The quartiles are Python's statistics.quantiles with method inclusive.
